description: Tactics2D is a Python simulation library by the Tactics2D research contributors for driving decision-making and reinforcement learning. It parses trajectory datasets and OpenDRIVE, Lanelet2-style OSM or SUMO maps, provides configurable vehicles and other participants, and supplies Gym-style road, intersection and parking scenarios. Outputs include trajectories, bird's-eye observations, simulated LiDAR and replay visualisations. Coverage follows user-selected maps and scenarios, with local road geometry and simulation timing, not a fixed global dataset. Public source, package installation and tutorials are free under GPL-3.0. A limitation is that original trajectory datasets are not redistributed and must be obtained under their providers' terms. The reviewed release supports Python 3.10–3.13 and excludes 3.14 because of dependencies. Tactics2D supports autonomous-driving simulations and complements SUMO (model-sumo). Although a separate branch supports a university course, the main resource is a documented research library with a 2024 IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Vehicles paper. No maps, trajectories, course materials or policy weights were downloaded.
